topup.title: Run out before the month does?
topup.body: Top-ups never expire, and are spent only once the plan's monthly credits are gone. Available from Starter upward.
packs: Or name your own amount, from $10

notes.title: Credits, not messages
notes.body: One credit is one input token of a baseline model. Every model spends credits in proportion to what it costs, so switching models changes the number — not the unit you are counting in.

notes.title: No surprise bills
notes.body: When the balance runs out, runs stop cleanly and say so. Nothing overruns quietly, and nothing is charged that was not spent.

notes.title: Change plan whenever
notes.body: Upgrade, downgrade or cancel from the billing screen. Your renewal date, what you have paid and every invoice are on the same page.

items.question: What exactly is a credit?
items.answer: One credit is one input token of a baseline model priced at $3 per million tokens. Every other model spends credits in proportion to what it actually costs — a cheap model spends a fraction of a credit per token, a frontier model spends several. Bought as a top-up, a million credits is $39; inside a plan they work out considerably cheaper.

items.question: How many tokens do my credits buy?
items.answer: It depends on the model, which is the point of counting in credits rather than tokens. An economy model stretches a million credits a long way; running Claude Opus on every step will spend them faster. Every run shows what it cost, step by step, and the usage screen adds it up by day, member and model.

items.question: What happens when I run out?
items.answer: Runs stop and say why. On a paid plan you can top up immediately or wait for the next monthly refill. Ragenta never keeps spending past the balance.

items.question: Does the free tier refill every month?
items.answer: No. Free is a trial: 20,000 credits once, granted when you verify your email address. What free is really for is trying the product on one knowledge base with a couple of agents — a monthly allowance that never ends would be a cost with no end for us and no reason to upgrade for you.

items.question: Do you train models on our data?
items.answer: No. Your documents and conversations are used to serve your workspace and nothing else. An Enterprise deployment can pin inference to your own endpoints so content never leaves your network.

items.question: Can we use our own models?
items.answer: Enterprise can point Ragenta at its own model endpoints, including self-hosted open-weights models. On every other plan an administrator chooses which of the catalogue's models each workspace may run.

lifecycle.title: The whole loop, in one system
lifecycle.subtitle: Ingest, retrieve, evaluate — and the evaluation feeds back into the first two.
lifecycle.planBody: Connect a source and Ragenta parses layout, chunks on structure, embeds and keeps it in sync — with the source's permissions attached.
planSteps: Chunk — on structure, not character count
lifecycle.designBody: Vector similarity and keyword matching run together, then a reranker orders what actually reaches the model's context.
lifecycle.validateBody: Groundedness, citation coverage and retrieval hit rate are scored on every change, so a regression surfaces before a user reports it.

capabilities.runToolsBody: Search your knowledge, query a database read-only, read a web page, work through a spreadsheet, send mail — with credentials held server-side and never shown to the model.
capabilities.addContextBody: Mention a document, a folder, a connector or a saved filter inline, and the agent scopes its retrieval to it for that run.
capabilities.snapshotsBody: Model, prompt, tools and each step's input and output are recorded against the version that produced them, so any answer can be read back exactly as it was produced — or compared against another version on the same question.

extend.skillsBody: Each template arrives as a working flow with its steps, tools and instructions already set — including what it must not do. Change what you need and publish a version of your own.

hero.subtitle: Your team asks the questions and makes the calls. Ragenta does the reading, the retrieval and the drafting.

items.title: Enterprise search
items.blurb: One search box across every system, answering in sentences instead of link lists.
items.challenge: Knowledge is spread across a wiki, a drive, a ticket system and three chat workspaces. People give up before they find it.
items.solution: Ragenta indexes them into one knowledge base and answers the question directly, with the passage it used attached. A connected account reads as the person who connected it, so an agent never sees more than they do.

items.title: Research assistant
items.blurb: Broad questions answered across many sources, with the evidence laid out.
items.challenge: Answering "what do we know about X" means reading twenty documents and hoping nothing was missed.
items.solution: An agent fans out across sources, covers each facet of the question, and shows which source supports which part of the answer.

items.title: Support deflection
items.blurb: Resolve repeat questions in-channel, escalate the rest with context attached.
items.challenge: Most tickets are answered by an article that already exists — but customers do not find it and agents retype it.
items.solution: A grounded agent answers from your help centre and policies, cites the article, and escalates with a summary when confidence is low.

items.title: RFPs & security questionnaires
items.blurb: Reuse every answer your team has already approved.
items.challenge: Each questionnaire repeats questions answered five times before, and the approved wording lives in someone's inbox.
items.solution: Ragenta matches each question to a previously approved answer with its source, and drafts only the genuine gaps for review.

items.title: IT & HR helpdesk
items.blurb: Policy answers posted into Slack, from the sources you scoped for that team.
items.challenge: HR and IT answer the same policy questions constantly, and the source of truth changes without anyone noticing.
items.solution: Answers come from the knowledge base you scoped for that team, and a connected account reads only what the person who connected it can read.

items.title: Analytics agent
items.blurb: Ask a metric question in words, get the query, the numbers and the caveats.
items.challenge: Every ad-hoc metric question becomes a ticket for the data team, and the backlog decides what gets answered.
items.solution: The agent writes read-only SQL against approved tables, runs it, and explains the result alongside the query it used.

items.title: Contract review
items.blurb: Every clause compared against your playbook, deviations ranked by risk.
items.challenge: First-pass review is slow, repetitive, and the thing that gets skipped when a deal is urgent.
items.solution: Ragenta parses the agreement into clauses, compares each against your standard position, and ranks deviations by exposure.

items.title: Compliance reporting
items.blurb: Evidence packages assembled from the systems of record.
items.challenge: Audit season means chasing screenshots and policy versions across half a dozen tools.
items.solution: An agent gathers the evidence, maps it to each control, and produces the package with a link to every underlying document.
